correctness.rationale: The source definitions give \(T(1)=\delta_0\), \(T(1/2)\) uniform on \(\{-1,1\}\), and \(T(2/5)\) uniform on \(\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}\). Their variances are exactly \(0\), \(1\), and \(2\). The variance function is continuous and strictly decreasing in \(\alpha\) on the source's piecewise definition, so \(1/2\) is the unique common parameter with variance \(1\). Exact convolution gives length-two concentrations \(2/5\) and \(3/8\), hence gap \(1/40\). All interval-boundary cases use the source's half-open convention.

value.rationale: This is a direct exact counterexample to an explicit open conjecture in the primary source. It occurs already for three summands and uses a natural special source distribution, \(T(2/5)\), which is uniform on five consecutive integers. The result identifies a concrete obstruction immediately beyond the symmetric three-point regime rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
